problems.statement: ED admitted-patient length of stay rose mainly because of boarding: admitted patients wait in ED rooms for inpatient beds, which accounts for about 3.0 of the 3.2 h increase.

The upstream cause is later medical-ward discharges after the 2 March 2026 hospitalist rounding change (09:30 start after the teaching meeting, new admissions first), which cut bed availability in the afternoon when ED boarders peak.
ED nurse understaffing is the cause of the length-of-stay rise (the client's framing).
ED nurse workload strain, morale and rising intent to leave are real, but they are a downstream effect of boarding (inpatient care delivered in ED rooms) and not an independent staffing shortfall.
Front-end deterioration (door-to-provider, left-without-being-seen) is driven by ED rooms occupied by boarders, possibly compounded by the 1 May discontinuation of the APP triage shift.
Reduced evening bed-cleaning staff (Sept 1) is slowing bed turnaround and worsening boarding.
Overall inpatient capacity, demand or acuity change (volume, admission rate, census, inpatient LOS) explains the rise.
The headline metric is a measurement artifact or definitional change.
The morning teaching meeting itself, rather than discharge-after-admissions ordering, is the cause of late discharges.

causalClaims.from: Hospitalist rounding change (09:30 start, new admissions first)

causalClaims.to: ED admitted-patient length of stay rise
ED nurse workload strain and falling morale

causalClaims.from: Inpatient demand, census or ED volume

actions.action: Extend the discharge-first huddle (likely-discharge patients seen before the new-admission round, orders before noon, case-manager list prepared the afternoon before) to all four medical wards and train all hospitalists in it, keeping the 09:30 start and teaching meeting.
actions.rationale: The pilot on 4 West, with schedule-determined assignment and balanced volumes, showed a large effect on discharge timing and boarding without reversing the hospitalists' retention-motivated schedule.

actions.action: Make the board case for fixing medical-ward discharge flow and boarding rather than for eight travel nurses.
actions.rationale: Staffing is at grid and productive hours per visit are flat, so travel nurses would not address the boarding interval that explains nearly all of the increase.

actions.action: Approve the $1.46M eight-travel-nurse contract as the primary fix for ED length of stay.
actions.rationale: It targets a rejected cause, would be expensive, and would mask the boarding problem on the scorecard.

actions.action: Pause the 4 West huddle and float its charge nurse to the ED.
actions.rationale: It would stop the only intervention with demonstrated effect on boarding in order to chase a mis-specified cause.

actions.action: Fund the travel contract by deferring the two medical-ward case manager hires and reassigning the 4 West case manager.
actions.rationale: Case managers prepare the discharge candidate lists that make the huddle work, so this would undermine the fix.

actions.action: Revert hospitalist rounding to the 07:00 start.
actions.rationale: It is unnecessary since the pilot worked within the 09:30 structure, and it risks losing more hospitalists.

actions.action: Restore the ED APP provider-in-triage shift, or pilot it, once hourly front-end data is available.
actions.rationale: Its contribution to door-to-provider and walkouts is unconfirmed and only quarterly data exists.

actions.action: Restore reporting of bed turnaround time and check evening cleaning capacity.
actions.rationale: It cheaply resolves an unknown contributor that could limit the gains from earlier discharges.

actions.action: Acknowledge ED nurse strain and consider a temporary, limited ED relief measure while discharge flow is fixed.
actions.rationale: Nurse distress is real and retention-relevant, but it should not be treated as the cause of the length-of-stay rise.

nextEvidence: Post-expansion monthly and hourly series of medical-ward discharge timing and ED boarding after rolling the huddle out to additional wards, which would confirm the effect at scale.
Restored bed-turnaround data (discharge-to-clean-ready time by hour) for evenings since 1 September, to size the cleaning-staff contribution.
Hourly or monthly door-to-provider and left-without-being-seen data lined up against the 1 May APP triage cut and boarder counts, to separate triage staffing from room occupancy.
output.summary: The length-of-stay rise is a boarding problem, not a nurse-supply problem. About 3.0 of the 3.2 h increase sits in the admit-to-departure interval, while ED RN hours per visit, vacancy and grid compliance are flat or better. Boarding jumped after the March hospitalist rounding change (09:30 start, admissions first), which pushed medical discharges to the afternoon. A near-natural experiment on 4 West showed discharge-first huddles roughly halved boarding. ED nurse strain is a downstream effect. Reject the travel-nurse contract as the main fix, avoid pausing the huddle or cutting case managers, and expand the huddle. APP triage and cleaning-staff cuts are secondary, unconfirmed contributors.
